article.dek: Rookie Jalon Daniels is expected to start for Tampa Bay and the app already prices him, the Value lane firmed up on the Chargers getting 7 in Seattle, and rain is in the forecast for Philadelphia and Baltimore.

items.headline: Rookie Jalon Daniels is expected to start for the Bucs — and the app already knows
paragraphs: Baker Mayfield is dealing with a thumb injury, and Tampa Bay is preparing rookie Jalon Daniels for a possible first start against Green Bay on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET. That is the biggest QB development of the morning, and it sits right on the 1 p.m. ET slate.

Here is the part that matters for you: the app's quarterback feed already lists Jalon Daniels as Tampa Bay's expected starter. You do not need to guess what the QB flip does to the number — the board did it for you. If the news firms up the other way before kickoff, remember the inactives timeline below.
items.takeaway: Daniels is expected to start for Tampa Bay on Sunday; the app's quarterback feed already reflects it, so the board's number already prices him in.

items.headline: The injury news, all in one place
paragraphs: Eagles vs. Rams (1 p.m. ET): Philadelphia is out without six players — DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Zack Baun (concussion), Marcus Epps (groin), Hollywood Brown, Dallas Goedert, and Fred Johnson. The Rams ruled out Aaron Donald, Jaylen Watson, and Terrance Ferguson; Puka Nacua practiced fully Friday and is on track to return, while tight end Colby Parkinson is questionable.

Ravens vs. Titans (1 p.m. ET): Baltimore ruled out both centers — Jovaughn Gwyn (ankle) and Ethan Pocic (knee) — plus edge rusher Trey Hendrickson (finger procedure). Rookie Vega Ioane is set to make his first start at center. Zay Flowers (hamstring), Chris Moore (ankle), and Ronnie Stanley (toe) are questionable. Tennessee listed Tyjae Spears and Kevin Winston Jr. as questionable.

London inactives are already out (9:30 a.m. ET kickoff): the Colts are without Keenan Allen (groin) with Ashton Dulin (ankle) questionable; the Commanders are without Jayden Daniels (elbow — Marcus Mariota starts), Sam Cosmi, Nick Cross, and Rachaad White, with Terry McLaurin (hamstring) and Percy Butler (concussion) questionable.
items.takeaway: Six Eagles out, both Ravens centers out with a rookie making his first start, and London's inactives are already official — Mariota starts for Washington.

items.headline: The forecast: rain in Philly and Baltimore, storms in Tampa, heat in Santa Clara
paragraphs: Kickoff-window weather for today's outdoor games, stated plainly: rain showers are likely in Philadelphia for Rams-Eagles (about 66°F, 56% chance of rain) and in Baltimore for Titans-Ravens (about 64°F, 55% chance). Tampa Bay could see scattered showers and storms for Packers-Bucs (about 88°F, 50% chance), and there is a chance of showers at MetLife for Cardinals-Giants (36%) and in Charlotte for Sunday night (45%).

Denver at San Francisco is the outlier the other way: about 96°F at Levi's Stadium at kickoff, near record territory. London was mild — about 57°F with light wind and a 15% chance of rain. Buffalo, Chicago, Cincinnati, and Seattle look clean.
items.takeaway: Wet in Philly and Baltimore, stormy in Tampa, very hot in Santa Clara — noted as fact, nothing more.

items.headline: Hit Rate: Buffalo, at -298
paragraphs: The Hit Rate lane has rotated. It is now Buffalo's moneyline at -298 on DraftKings, and the app gives the Bills a 71.2% chance of beating New England at home at 1 p.m. ET.

Hit Rate is the lane that forgoes value for win probability — which supported pick looks most likely to win. The app's own tutorial says it straight: Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate. At -298, every $2.98 you risk wins $1. You are paying for the win probability, and the card is honest about what you are buying.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate is Buffalo's moneyline at -298 — a 71.2% model chance, priced like a favorite, because that is what this lane is for.

items.headline: Balanced: the Eagles lay 3.5 at home
paragraphs: The middle lane is Philadelphia -3.5 against the Rams, -105 at FanDuel, with the app giving the Eagles a 50.5% chance of covering. Balanced is the strong-pick-without-overpaying lane — the good starting point if you are newer to this.

That 50.5% is the app's number against a Rams team getting Puka Nacua back, with both teams down starters. The lane is not a claim that 3.5 is a bargain. It is the middle ground: real support, reasonable price.
items.takeaway: Balanced is Eagles -3.5 at home — the middle lane, a supported pick at a fair price, not a value claim.

items.headline: Value: the Chargers lane got real
paragraphs: The Value lane is the Chargers +7 at Seattle, -105 on DraftKings, and it firmed up overnight: the app's expected value went from a whisper-thin +0.31% last night to +2.38% this morning, with the model giving the Chargers a 50.45% chance of covering 7.

Value is always the model's +EV play — the book's price is cheaper than the app's price. +2.38% means that over many bets at this price the math expects a gain. It does not mean this one wins. That is what the lane is: the best price on the board, judged by the model, one bet at a time.
items.takeaway: Value is Chargers +7 at Seattle at -105 — the model's +EV play, firmed from +0.31% to +2.38% overnight.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Overnight: Buffalo took the top lane, the Value lane firmed up
paragraphs: Two real changes on the morning board, both from the 6:00 refresh. First, the Hit Rate lane rotated off Chicago — the Bagent moneyline from last night is gone — and onto Buffalo's moneyline at -298. The board re-ran the whole slate overnight and Buffalo came out on top of the win-probability lane.
Second, the Value lane got stronger on the same ticket: Chargers +7 at Seattle went from +0.31% expected value last night to +2.38% this morning at -105. Same line, better price math.

If your book is not DraftKings or FanDuel, or the line has moved since the morning refresh, do not take the card's price as yours. Tap Check in the app, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on YOUR price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: The board rotated overnight: Hit Rate is Buffalo now, and the Chargers value read tripled in strength on the same +7. Use Check for your own book's price.

items.headline: Inactives: London's are out, the 1 p.m. ET games report at about 11:30
paragraphs: London's inactives already landed — see the injury section. For the rest of today's games, inactives come out about 90 minutes before kickoff, so the 1 p.m. ET games report around 11:30 a.m. ET.

The names to watch when the 1 p.m. ET inactives drop: Zay Flowers, Chris Moore, and Ronnie Stanley for Baltimore, Colby Parkinson for the Rams, and Ashton Dulin for the Colts. Questionable is not out. Check the official inactives, then check the app — the board refreshes every morning and evening, and anything that lands after the refresh is what Check is for.
items.takeaway: 1 p.m. ET inactives land around 11:30 a.m. ET — watch the questionable tags, then let Check re-run your price if anything changed.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: spread
paragraphs: The spread is the head start the book gives the underdog — or the deficit it assigns the favorite — to make a lopsided game bettable. Chargers +7 means the Chargers can lose by up to 6 points and your bet still wins; if they lose by exactly 7, it is a push and your stake comes back.

A morning note on the Fade: I checked the VSiN betting-splits free tier this morning and the featured free row was a college game, with no NFL featured row visible — and DraftKings-only splits alone are never enough to call a Fade. So no Fade today. The jargon item stands in its place, as it should.
items.takeaway: Spread = the underdog's head start. Chargers +7: lose by 6 or less and you cash, lose by exactly 7 and it's a push. No Fade today — no verified split.

items.headline: The tracker only works if you are honest with yourself
paragraphs: A quick nudge, because it matters: settlement is manual. There is no auto-settle sweeping up your results — the tracker only knows what you tell it. Log the losers too. A record that only has winners in it is not a record, it is a highlight reel, and highlight reels do not teach you anything.
items.takeaway: Log every bet, winners and losers — the tracker only works if you are honest with it.
